criteria.description: The theorem statements and proof arguments are internally consistent, use the frozen Farey and gap conventions, handle edge cases and normalizations, and do not promote numerical evidence into proof.

The work derives a substantive result directly from prime-denominator Farey insertions and the per-step shift, including a quantitative shear law and the triangular shift law with the claimed moments.

The gap-permutation theorem rigorously proves the qualitative two-sided sigma_g N^(3/2) law with explicit constants, correctly distinguishes this from Garcia's sharper provisional constants, and states the averaging convention for repeated gaps.

A practical application follows from the theorem itself: it replaces factorial permutation enumeration with an O(N) certificate, reports exact quantities and rigorous bounds, and keeps the narrower coprime-layer optimizer's negative controls visible.

Classical finite-population moments and one-dimensional discrepancy identities are credited, bounded-search novelty is not presented as exhaustive priority, and the defensible new contribution is isolated from its classical ingredients.

The manuscript identifies independently checkable formulas, computational certificates, application interfaces, tests, limitations, and enough implementation detail for another researcher to reproduce or falsify the claims.
The manuscript clearly separates proved project results, computer-assisted corollaries, failed conjectures, practical scope limits, and external-priority claims still requiring specialist review.
